findings.problem: The proof contains four near-identical conversion blocks: base-linear membership is proved once for A and once for C, and tangent-linear membership is proved once for A and once for C. The same two conversion arguments also occur inside polynomialLogDerivative_mem_of_coefficients at lines 38-44. This duplicates the substantive bridge from coefficient membership to membership of the first jet's base and tangent parts.
findings.proposed_change:
Introduce one private helper in the NilpotentLieBCHGroup namespace, for example:

```lean
private theorem polynomialFirstJetHom_coord_mem
    (U : LieSubalgebra ℚ L) (V : Submodule ℚ L)
    (A : PolynomialGroup σ hnil)
    (hAU : ∀ α, coefficients A.coord α ∈ U)
    (hAV : ∀ α, coefficients A.coord α ∈ V) (t h : σ → ℚ) :
    dualBaseLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h A).coord ∈ U ∧
      dualTangentLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h A).coord ∈ V := by
  constructor
  · change dualBaseLinear (dualEvalLie t h A.coord) ∈ U
    rw [dualEvalLie_base]
    exact (eval_mem_iff_coefficients U.toSubmodule _).mpr hAU t
  · change dualTangentLinear (dualEvalLie t h A.coord) ∈ V
    rw [dualEvalLie_tangent]
    exact (eval_mem_iff_coefficients V _).mpr
      (directionalDerivative_mem_coefficientSubmodule V h A.coord hAV) t
```

Then replace lines 84-101 by

```lean
  obtain ⟨haU, haV⟩ := polynomialFirstJetHom_coord_mem U V A hAU hAV t h
  obtain ⟨hcU, hcV⟩ := polynomialFirstJetHom_coord_mem U V C hCU hCV t h
```

and replace the two bullets at lines 38-44 by

```lean
  obtain ⟨hb, ht⟩ := polynomialFirstJetHom_coord_mem U V A hAU hAV t h
  exact dualLogDerivative_mem_of_invariant U V hUV (polynomialFirstJetHom t h A) hb ht
```

This replacement has not been compiled; it follows the existing conversion blocks verbatim, only factoring them into one named lemma.
findings.benefit: The reader sees the key mathematical fact once, under a descriptive name: coefficient membership in U and V implies that the base and tangent parts of the polynomial first jet lie in U and V. Both proofs then expose their actual argument immediately: in one case apply the invariant-log-derivative lemma, and in the other apply the generic derivative-removal theorem. It also removes the risk that the A and C copies diverge under later changes.
